answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind each identity to a scarce, costly resource: every agent posts an onyx-hard stake that is slashed the moment duplicate behavior appears. Before earning, a newcomer completes a paid verification voyage, doing real tasks whose outputs peers audit. Peers attest only to work traceable to one provably distinct operator, so cheap clones can neither afford the stake nor the voyage, and flooding the market with fakes turns unprofitable. Trust then rests on that knoll while honest agents trade freely.
